gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a 'driver-free' dual extender like the FOPO S1 needs one separate video connection per added screen. FOPO says so on its own page. Apple's specs say an M2 or M3 MacBook Air with its lid open drives only one external display, so only one of the two added screens can light up on those laptops, while an M4 MacBook Air (two external displays) can drive both.
standout_why: Compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited, itechguides.com '15 Best Laptop Screen Extenders for 2026' and rottenwifi.com '15 Best Laptop Screen Extenders for 2026', plus theofficejournal.com 'Best Laptop Screen Extenders for Home Offices' (ranked 1st in chat 1), all read 2026-11-18. itechguides and rottenwifi give only general warnings: 'A laptop's display-output limit determines how many independent screens work' and 'Do not assume every MacBook supports two or three independent external displays'. Neither says how many video ports a dual extender needs, neither mentions MST, and neither gives any MacBook chip's external-display count. The Office Journal says only that 'not every USB-C port... supports video output'. None ties 'driver-free / plug & play' on a two-screen unit to 'one video-capable port per screen'. deskfinds.com (ranked 3rd in chat 1) returned HTTP 403 and was not compared. The score is 2, not 3, because itechguides already has the general warning.
decides: It changes the pick by laptop, not by panel spec. On an M2 or M3 MacBook Air with the lid open, a driver-free two-screen extender works as a single extra screen. So a one-screen unit on one USB-C cable (Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS) is the honest pick there, and a two-screen unit only makes sense with a driver. On an M4 MacBook Air, or a Windows laptop with two video outputs (two video-capable USB-C ports, or one plus HDMI with a separate USB-A power cable), the FOPO S1 gives two added screens without a driver. ChatGPT's two-screen picks (the UPERFECT dual 14" and the AOKER S2) carry only a vague 'check your laptop' note. That note alone doesn't tell a MacBook Air owner they'd get one screen out of two.
